I don't know, man, I want to see a peer review on this. It seems like it would add a ton of weight to the aircraft.

I'd fly on it, but not because I think it's particularly safer than any other design. The article cites 10 accidents per million as its bragging point, though, so I can't see airlines plunking money down on something like this. Especially since most accidents that result in crashes are either so catastrophic that a feature like this wouldn't help, or are simply the result of malice, to which the same logic applies.

If you wanted to pull off something like this and be successful, you'd have to design a highly modular fuselage. Reason being, the fuselage being the largest part of the aircraft, it's likely to take the brunt of the damage in any catastrophic failure or act of malice, mentioned above. With a highly modular fuselage, say perhaps ten separate cabin sections that could be deployed, each with their own drop system, you'd stand a much greater chance of at least some of the passengers surviving even terrible damage to the cabin, as it would be unlikely to impact all ten sections.
